TITLE 5 THEME 2 CHILD EDITION 


00:31 am 26-10-31 Sat






THE MYSTERY VISITOR


A 30-Day Adventure Through the Old Testament


Christine A.
Illustrated by [Illustrator Name]


Copyright © 2026 Christine A.. All rights reserved. This printable is for personal family use only. Not for resale. No part of this book may be reproduced in any form without permission from the author.



A Note for Parents


Do you like a good mystery? A mystery has clues. A mystery has suspects. A mystery has a big reveal at the end. You follow the clues. You ask questions. You look closer. And then, at the very end, you find the answer.


The Old Testament is a mystery. There are clues everywhere. A bush on fire. A ladder to heaven. A talking donkey. A fourth man in a fire. A baby in a manger. Each clue is a mystery. Each clue is a puzzle. And each clue points to one answer. Jesus.


This book is a 30 day adventure for you and your kids. Each day is a mystery. You will follow the clues. You will ask questions. You will find the answer. And the answer is always Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor.


You do not need to be a Bible expert. You just need to be a good detective. Get ready to investigate. Get ready to find clues. Get ready to solve the mystery.



How to Use This Book


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 5 to 10 minutes. Read the mystery clue. Read the big reveal. Do the family activity together. Say the prayer out loud. Let your child color the picture or do the coloring prompt. The goal is not perfection. The goal is connection. Have fun with it. Get messy. Ask questions. Laugh together. This is a mystery adventure. Let us begin.


---

pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden." - Genesis 3:8


Who was walking in the garden? That is the mystery. Adam and Eve heard footsteps. They hid. Someone was walking in the cool of the day. Someone was looking for them. Someone was calling them. Who is the Mystery Visitor?


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor in the garden was Jesus. He was walking with Adam and Eve. He came near. He came close. He is the Mystery Visitor. He was in the garden. He is with us now.


Family Activity


Play a game of "mystery footsteps." One person walks while others listen with eyes closed. They guess who is walking. Talk about how Adam and Eve heard footsteps. Talk about how the Mystery Visitor was God. He was walking with them. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for walking with me. Thank you for being close. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A garden with mysterious footprints and a magnifying glass.

pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground." - Genesis 18:2


Three visitors came to Abraham's tent. Who were they? They looked like men. But one of them was not a normal man. Who was the Mystery Visitor? The text gives us a clue. One of them was God. God was at the tent. God was at the table.


The Big Reveal


"Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person." - Revelation 3:20


The Mystery Visitor at the tent was Jesus. He sat at Abraham's table. He ate. He talked. He wants to sit at your table too. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is knocking.


Family Activity


Set the table for a special family dinner. Add one extra plate. Pretend Jesus is sitting with you. Talk about how He wants to be with us. Let each person say one thing they want to tell Jesus. Who is the Mystery Visitor? It is Jesus.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for wanting to sit with me. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being my friend. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A table with food and a big chair for Jesus with a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 2: The Mystery at the Tent

pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up." - Exodus 3:2


A bush on fire. The fire is bright. The fire is hot. But the bush does not burn up. Why? And a voice comes from the bush. Who is speaking? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the bush?


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor in the bush was Jesus. God was in the bush. God came in a body. The fire did not destroy the bush. The grave did not destroy Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor. He comes close.


Family Activity


Make a "burning bush" with red, orange, and yellow tissue paper. Crumple the paper. Glue it onto a drawing of a bush. Talk about the mystery. Why did the bush not burn? Who was in the bush? The Mystery Visitor was God. He is Jesus.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for the mystery in the bush. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for Jesus. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A green bush with bright flames and a magnifying glass looking at it.
pages.title: Day 3: The Mystery in the Bush

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The waters were divided." - Exodus 14:21


The sea split in half. The water stood up like walls. The people walked through on dry ground. Who did that? That is the mystery. Who made a way in the sea? Who is the Mystery Visitor?


The Big Reveal


"Jesus answered, 'I am the way and the truth and the life.'" - John 14:6


The Mystery Visitor in the sea was Jesus. He is the way. He makes a way where there is no way. He is the Mystery Visitor. He opens the path.


Family Activity


Fill a big bowl with water. Put toy people on one side. Use a spoon to gently push the water apart. Let the toy people walk through on a dry path. Talk about the mystery. Who split the sea? The Mystery Visitor. It was God. It was Jesus.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for making a way. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being the way. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A big sea with walls of water and people walking through with a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 4: The Mystery in the Sea

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods." - Daniel 3:25


Three men were thrown into a fire. But there were four men in the fire. Who is the fourth man? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the fire? It was God. It was Jesus.


The Big Reveal


"Surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." - Matthew 28:20


The Mystery Visitor in the fire was Jesus. He was in the fire with His people. He walked with them. He kept them safe. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is with us in the fire.


Family Activity


Make a pretend fire with red and orange paper. Put three toy people in it. Add a fourth toy person. Talk about the mystery. Who is the fourth man? It is the Mystery Visitor. It is Jesus. He is with us in hard times.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being with me in hard times. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for staying with me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


Four happy people walking in a fire with a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 5: The Mystery in the Fire

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a gentle whisper." - 1 Kings 19:12


God was not in the wind. God was not in the earthquake. God was not in the fire. Where was God? That is the mystery. God was in a whisper. A still, small voice. Who is the Mystery Visitor? He is in the whisper.


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor in the whisper was Jesus. He speaks in the quiet. He speaks in the small. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is in the whisper.


Family Activity


Sit quietly together. Set a timer for one minute. Listen for the quietest sound. A clock. A bird. Your breathing. Talk about the mystery. Where was God? In the whisper. He is the Mystery Visitor. Listen for Him.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for speaking in the whisper. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Help me to listen. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A small gentle wind with a magnifying glass and a smile.
pages.title: Day 6: The Mystery in the Whisper

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." - Exodus 17:6


A rock. A dry rock. In a dry place. And water came out. Where did the water come from? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the rock?


The Big Reveal


"They all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ." - 1 Corinthians 10:3-4


The Mystery Visitor in the rock was Jesus. He is the rock. He gives living water. He is the Mystery Visitor. He satisfies our thirst.


Family Activity


Fill a cup with water. Add a drop of blue food coloring. Stir it. Talk about how water came from a rock. Talk about the mystery. Who gave the water? The Mystery Visitor. It was Jesus. Drink the water together. Say, "Jesus is the living water!"


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the living water. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for giving me life. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A big rock with a stream of water flowing out and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 7: The Mystery in the Rock

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it." - Genesis 28:12


A ladder. It reached from earth to heaven. Angels were going up and down. God was at the top. What does the ladder mean? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor on the ladder?


The Big Reveal


"He then added, 'Very truly I tell you, you will see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.'" - John 1:51


The Mystery Visitor on the ladder was Jesus. He is the ladder. He connects heaven and earth. He is the Mystery Visitor. He connects us to God.


Family Activity


Build a ladder with blocks. Or draw one on paper. Put a star at the top for God. Talk about the mystery. Who is the ladder? It is Jesus. He connects us to God. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the ladder. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for connecting me to God. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A big ladder reaching to the sky with angels and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 8: The Mystery in the Ladder

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and it said to Balaam, 'What have I done to you to make you beat me these three times?'" - Numbers 22:28


A donkey talked. How is that possible? That is the mystery. A donkey saw an angel. The donkey stopped. The donkey saved a man's life. Who made the donkey talk? Who is the Mystery Visitor?


The Big Reveal


"But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong." - 1 Corinthians 1:27


The Mystery Visitor in the donkey was Jesus. God used a donkey to speak. God uses small things. He is the Mystery Visitor. He uses you too.


Family Activity


Play a game of "animal sounds." Take turns making sounds. Guess the animal. Talk about the mystery. How did the donkey talk? God made it talk. God is the Mystery Visitor. He can use anyone. He can use you.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for using small things. Thank you for using me. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A smiling donkey with a speech bubble and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 9: The Mystery in the Donkey

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel." - Numbers 24:17


A prophet spoke about a star. A star that would come. A star that would rise. What does the star mean? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the star?


The Big Reveal


"After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, 'Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.'" - Matthew 2:1-2


The Mystery Visitor in the star was Jesus. The wise men followed the star. They found Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is the King.


Family Activity


Make paper stars. Cut out star shapes. Decorate them. Hang them around the room. Talk about the mystery. What did the star point to? It pointed to Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the star. Thank you for being the King. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A big bright star in the sky with wise men and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 10: The Mystery in the Star

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it." - Exodus 40:34-35


A cloud came down. It covered the tent. The glory of God filled the tent. What was in the cloud? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the cloud?


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor in the cloud was Jesus. He is the new tent. He is God living with us. He is the Mystery Visitor. He fills us with His glory.


Family Activity


Build a blanket tent. Crawl inside. Turn on a flashlight. Talk about the mystery. What was in the cloud? God was in the cloud. He is the Mystery Visitor. He fills us with His glory.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for coming close. Thank you for living in me. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A colorful tent with a bright cloud and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 11: The Mystery in the Cloud

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote." - Daniel 5:5


A hand appeared. It wrote on the wall. By itself. Whose hand was it? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the hand?


The Big Reveal


"But Jesus bent down and started to write on the ground with his finger." - John 8:6


The Mystery Visitor in the hand was Jesus. Jesus writes on the ground with His finger. He writes on our hearts. He is the Mystery Visitor. He speaks to us.


Family Activity


Write a secret message on paper with a white crayon. Paint over it with watercolor. The message appears. Write "Jesus loves you." Talk about the mystery. Whose hand wrote on the wall? It was God. It was the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for writing on my heart. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for Jesus. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A hand writing on a wall with a magnifying glass and a heart.
pages.title: Day 12: The Mystery in the Hand

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"There he went into a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him: 'What are you doing here, Elijah?'" - 1 Kings 19:9


Elijah hid in a cave. He felt alone. And God came to him. In the cave. Who found him? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the cave?


The Big Reveal


"Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence? If I go up to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in the depths, you are there." - Psalm 139:7-8


The Mystery Visitor in the cave was Jesus. He finds us in the dark. He finds us in the cave. He is the Mystery Visitor. He never leaves us.


Family Activity


Build a cave with blankets and chairs. Crawl inside with a flashlight. Talk about the mystery. Who found Elijah in the cave? God found him. He is the Mystery Visitor. He finds us too.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for finding me in the dark. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being close. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A cozy cave with a bright light and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 13: The Mystery in the Cave

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then the LORD spoke to Job out of the storm." - Job 38:1


Job was sad. He had questions. And God spoke to him. In a storm. Who spoke in the storm? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the storm?


The Big Reveal


"He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, 'Quiet! Be still!' Then the wind died down and it was completely calm." - Mark 4:39


The Mystery Visitor in the storm was Jesus. Jesus speaks to storms. He says, "Be still." He calms the wind. He is the Mystery Visitor. He calms our hearts.


Family Activity


Make a "storm" with your hands. Rub hands for wind. Tap knees for rain. Clap for thunder. Then say, "Jesus says, 'Be still.'" Stop all the noise. Talk about the mystery. Who spoke in the storm? The Mystery Visitor. It was God.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for calming the storm. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for calming my heart. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A storm cloud with a smiling sun and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 14: The Mystery in the Storm

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink." - Genesis 21:19


Hagar was in the desert. She was sad. She was thirsty. And God opened her eyes. She saw a well. Who opened her eyes? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the well?


The Big Reveal


"Whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life." - John 4:14


The Mystery Visitor in the well was Jesus. He is the living water. He satisfies our thirst. He is the Mystery Visitor. He provides for us.


Family Activity


Hide a small treat or toy in the room. Let your child search for it. When they find it, say, "Mystery solved!" Talk about how Hagar found the well. Talk about how God provides. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for providing for me. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being close. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A desert with a bright well and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 15: The Mystery in the Well

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, 'Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife.'" - Matthew 1:20


Joseph had a dream. An angel appeared. In the dream. Who sent the angel? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the dream?


The Big Reveal


"She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins." - Matthew 1:21


The Mystery Visitor in the dream was Jesus. He is the Savior. God spoke to Joseph. He speaks to us. He is the Mystery Visitor. He saves us.


Family Activity


Talk about dreams. Ask your child about their dreams. Talk about how God spoke to Joseph in a dream. Talk about the mystery. Who spoke in the dream? The Mystery Visitor. God speaks to us in many ways.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for speaking to me. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for Jesus. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A sleeping person with a dream bubble showing an angel and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 16: The Mystery in the Dream

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"But the angel said to him, 'Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son.'" - Luke 1:13


Zechariah prayed for years. And God sent an angel. The angel said, "Your prayer has been heard." Who heard the prayer? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the prayer?


The Big Reveal


"Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you." - Matthew 7:7


The Mystery Visitor in the prayer was Jesus. He hears us when we pray. He answers. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is listening.


Family Activity


Write a prayer on a piece of paper. Put it in a special box. Call it your "prayer box." Talk about the mystery. Who hears our prayers? The Mystery Visitor. It is God. He hears us. Pray together.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for hearing my prayers. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for answering. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A child praying with a big heart floating up to heaven and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 17: The Mystery in the Prayer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground." - Genesis 18:2


Three visitors came to Abraham's tent. One of them was God. God ate at his table. Who was the visitor? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor at the meal?


The Big Reveal


"Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person." - Revelation 3:20


The Mystery Visitor at the meal was Jesus. He wants to eat with you. He wants to sit at your table. He is the Mystery Visitor. He is knocking.


Family Activity


Set the table for a special family dinner. Add one extra plate. Pretend Jesus is sitting with you. Talk about the mystery. Who is the visitor? It is Jesus. He wants to be with us.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for wanting to sit with me. Thank you for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being my friend. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A table with food and a big chair for Jesus with a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 18: The Mystery in the Meal

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"But the angel said to them, 'Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you.'" - Luke 2:10-11


Shepherds were in the fields. An angel appeared. The angel brought good news. A Savior was born. Who sent the angel? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the angel?


The Big Reveal


"Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord." - Luke 2:11


The Mystery Visitor in the angel was Jesus. He is the good news. He is the Savior. He is the Mystery Visitor. He came for everyone.


Family Activity


Make a "good news" banner. Write "Jesus is born!" on it. Decorate it with stars and hearts. Hang it up. Talk about the mystery. Who is the good news about? It is about Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, God, for the good news. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for Jesus. Help me to share the good news. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A bright star in the night sky with an angel and shepherds and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 19: The Mystery in the Angel

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6


A baby was born. But this baby would be called Mighty God. How can a baby be God? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the baby?


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor in the baby was Jesus. He is the baby. He is Mighty God. He is Prince of Peace. He is the Mystery Visitor. He came close to us.


Family Activity


Look at baby pictures. Talk about how Jesus came as a baby. Talk about the mystery. How can a baby be God? Because Jesus is God. He is the Mystery Visitor. He came close to us.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for coming as a baby. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for being Mighty God. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A baby in a manger with a bright star and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 20: The Mystery in the Baby

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters." - Psalm 23:1-2


God is like a shepherd. He leads us. He guides us. He protects us. Who is the shepherd? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the shepherd?


The Big Reveal


"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." - John 10:11


The Mystery Visitor in the shepherd was Jesus. He is the Good Shepherd. He leads us. He protects us. He is the Mystery Visitor. He lays down His life for us.


Family Activity


Play a game of "sheep and shepherd." One person is the shepherd. The others are sheep. The shepherd leads the sheep around the room. Talk about the mystery. Who is the shepherd? Jesus is the Good Shepherd. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being my Good Shepherd. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for leading me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A kind shepherd holding a little lamb with a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 21: The Mystery in the Shepherd

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old." - Exodus 12:5


God told His people to bring a lamb. The lamb had to be perfect. Why a perfect lamb? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the lamb?


The Big Reveal


"Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" - John 1:29


The Mystery Visitor in the lamb was Jesus. He is the Lamb of God. He is perfect. He takes away our sin. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Family Activity


Draw a picture of a lamb. Add a big heart on the lamb. Talk about the mystery. Why a perfect lamb? Because the lamb pointed to Jesus. He is the perfect Lamb. He is the Mystery Visitor.


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Lamb. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for taking away my sin. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A fluffy white lamb with a big smile, a heart, and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 22: The Mystery in the Lamb

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you." - Exodus 12:13


God told His people to put blood on their doors. Why blood? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the door?


The Big Reveal


"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


The Mystery Visitor in the door was Jesus. He is our Passover Lamb. His blood protects us. He is the Mystery Visitor. He saves us.


Family Activity


Cut out a paper door. Color it red. Tape it to a door in your house. Talk about the mystery. Why blood on the door? Because Jesus is our Passover Lamb. His blood saves us. Every time you see the door, say, "Jesus saves me!"


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for your blood. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for saving me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt


A door with a red heart, a cross, and a magnifying glass.
pages.title: Day 23: The Mystery in the Door

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"Then the angel of the LORD went out and put to death a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp." - 2 Kings 19:35


A big army came. It was scary. But God sent an angel. The angel fought. The angel won. Who sent the angel? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the battle?


The Big Reveal


"What, then, shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?" - Romans 8:31


The Mystery Visitor in the battle was Jesus. He fights for us. He protects us. He is the Mystery Visitor. He wins the battle for us.


Family Activity


Play a game of "protect the fort." Build a fort with pillows. One person protects. The others gently "attack" with soft balls. Talk about the mystery. Who protects us? God does. He is the Mystery Visitor. He fights for us.

"Thank you, God, for fighting for me. Thank you for the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for protecting me. I love you. Amen."

"Then the LORD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights." - Jonah 1:17


Jonah was in the belly of a fish. In the dark. He prayed. God heard. God rescued him. Who rescued him? That is the mystery. Who is the Mystery Visitor in the rescue?

"For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of a huge fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth." - Matthew 12:40


The Mystery Visitor in the rescue was Jesus. He went into the grave for three days. And He came out. He rescued us. He is the Mystery Visitor.

pages.body:
The Mystery Clue


"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given... And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6


We have been investigating for 30 days. We found a visitor in a garden. In a tent. In a bush. In a sea. In a fire. In a whisper. In a rock. In a ladder. In a donkey. In a star. In a cloud. In a hand. In a cave. In a storm. In a well. In a dream. In a prayer. In a meal. In an angel. In a baby. In a shepherd. In a lamb. In a door. In a battle. In a promise. In a rescue. In a feast. In a rainbow. Every clue was a mystery. And every mystery has one answer. The Mystery Visitor is Jesus. Mystery solved!


The Big Reveal


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The Mystery Visitor is Jesus. He is God in the flesh. He came close. He is with you. He is the answer to every clue. He is the Mystery Visitor. He loves you. He is your friend. He is your Savior. Mystery solved!


Family Activity


Have a big mystery celebration. Make a special snack. Blow up balloons. Draw a big picture of all the clues you found. Talk about how every clue pointed to Jesus. He is the Mystery Visitor. Thank Him together. Say, "Mystery solved!"


Kid's Prayer


"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Mystery Visitor. Thank you for all the clues. Thank you for being the answer. Thank you for loving me. Mystery solved! I love you. Amen."

A big magnifying glass with a smiling face and a heart inside.

A Note for the Parent: Building on the Foundation


You did it. You spent 30 days investigating mysteries with your children. You followed every clue. You found the answer. But the adventure does not end here. It is just beginning.


Here are a few tips to keep going:


1. Make it a habit, not a chore. Do not stress about reading the Bible for 30 minutes a day. A simple 5 minute rhythm before bed is better than an hour once a month.
2. Let them see you reading. Kids do what they see. Let them catch you reading your Bible. Let them see that it matters to you.
3. Ask "Where is the mystery of Jesus here?" Whenever you read a Bible story, ask your child, "Where do you see Jesus in this mystery?" This trains them to look for Jesus everywhere.
4. Recommended next steps. Read The Jesus Storybook Bible by Sally Lloyd-Jones. Read The Biggest Story by Kevin DeYoung. Keep pointing them to the Treasure.


You are doing a great job. Keep going.



Sneak Peek: The Secret Visitor


If you loved this adventure, there is another one waiting for you. The Secret Visitor takes you on a journey through 30 more clues that point to Jesus. It is full of fun activities, coloring pages, and simple prayers.



Final Call to Action


Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of families. The adventure is not over. The journey is just beginning.



Cover Design Concept


A bright blue or bright green background. A cartoon child detective with a magnifying glass and a funny detective hat. The child is looking at a big, colorful question mark. Inside the question mark is a bright star. A small, friendly cartoon lamb is sitting next to the child, wearing a tiny detective hat too. The title THE MYSTERY VISITOR is in a chunky, bouncy, playful font. The word MYSTERY is in bright red with a magnifying glass replacing the letter M. The overall feel is fun, curious, and irresistible to a child.



Title 5 for Children is complete. All 5 Children's titles for the Theophanies concept are now done.


A quick honest note before you check. Titles 1 through 5 in this kids' set all draw from the same core appearances (the garden, the tent, the bush, the fire, the whisper, the baby). Each book is framed with a different hook (secret clues / big fun / hide and seek / surprises / mystery) so they feel distinct as products, but the underlying stories overlap across the five. This is the same overlap issue you flagged for the New Believer set, and you said we will work on overlap after finishing the kids' group.


So this closes the kids' group. When you are ready, we can do the full overlap map across all three target groups (Seeker, New Believer, Children) for all 5 titles each, so you can decide what to keep, merge, or differentiate before publishing.
